## How we work (AI-native loop)
- Each change lives in `changes/<slug>/` (intent.md → spec.md → plan.md) on branch `change/<slug>`. Each stage ends by committing its artifact; the next one reads it.
- Gates are human: the Product Owner accepts the intent, PO + policy owners approve the spec, the engineer/tech lead approves the plan. The agent never approves for a person (`sdlc approve` or the `sdlc ui` dashboard). With `risk.profile: graded`, `sdlc approve <change> <spec|plan> --auto` records the approval only when the risk tier needs nobody.
- Nothing is implemented without an approved `plan.md`. If the implementation deviates, update `plan.md` in the same commit. Exception: the person explicitly asks for a small change outside the loop; do it and say it has no traceability.
- Small, low-risk changes: quick lane (`sdlc quick "<what>"`, then /sdlc-quick), no spec or plan; the limits (`quick_lane`, high-risk paths) are checked on every push. Beyond them: `sdlc promote`.
- During a fix (`sdlc lock on`) tests are not edited: failing test first, then the code.
- Always verify with `.sdlc/config.json → commands` before calling something done.
- Loop status: `sdlc status`; what next: `sdlc next`. Guardrails: if a hook or git hook blocks, do not work around it; read the message.

### Stages
- **sdlc-discovery** — Discovery stage of the AI-native loop (experimental). → `.agents/skills/sdlc-discovery/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-roadmap** — Stage 0 of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-roadmap/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-intent** — Stage 1 (Plan) of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-intent/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-spec** — Stage 2 (Design) of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-spec/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-plan** — Stage 3 (Build) of the AI-native loop, first half. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-plan/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-build** — Stage 3 (Build) of the AI-native loop, second half. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-build/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-fix** — Stage 4 (Test) of the AI-native loop for bugs. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-fix/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-quick** — Quick lane of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-quick/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-ship** — Stage 5 (Deploy) of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-ship/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-status** — Shows which stage of the AI-native loop each change (changes/*) is at, the state of its PR/MR and its Jira ticket, flags inconsistencies and suggests the next command. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-status/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-incident** — Stage 6 (Maintain) of the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-incident/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-explain** — Writes or refreshes the explainer of one module in docs/explainers/ — what it does, its architecture, the invariants the code relies on and the risks of changing it, each with file:line evidence. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-explain/SKILL.md`
- **sdlc-setup** — Walkthrough that gets a project ready to work in the AI-native loop. → `.agents/skills/sdlc-setup/SKILL.md`
- **policy-secure-api** — Applies the organization's API security standard. → `.agents/skills/policy-secure-api/SKILL.md`

### Guardrails (no hooks stop you here: you enforce them)
- Protected paths, never edited by hand: `src/gen/**`, `**/*.generated.ts`. If one has to change: a generated file is regenerated from its source (edit the generator and run it); an applied migration is corrected with a new migration.
- Production gate: never run commands matching `deploy.*prod`, `terraform apply`, `kubectl .*--context[= ].*prod`, even when asked. Stop and ask a person to run it with `RELEASE_APPROVAL` set.
- Secrets: never write credentials, tokens or keys in code or committed files; read them from the environment.
- Test-lock: while `sdlc lock status` is ON, do not edit `test/**`, `**/*.test.ts`.
- Git hooks (pre-commit) check the same on commit: if they block, fix the change; never use `--no-verify`.

When the user asks for a stage (by name or with `/sdlc-<stage>`), read and follow the matching skill. For clean-context reviews (verifier, spec-reviewer, simplifier, researcher), use `.agents/agents/<name>.md`.
